models_evaluated: three instruction-tuned language models (not named in the abstract)

links.outcome: risk-bearing language in hallucinated, weakly grounded LLM patient-facing medical answers across three models
links.effect: Models with similar surface-level behavior showed substantially different risk profiles; standard metrics did not capture these differences. No numbers are reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Our results show that models with similar surface-level behavior exhibit substantially different risk profiles and that standard evaluation metrics fail to capture these distinctions.

unlisted_practices: Risk-sensitive hallucination scoring based on risk-bearing language (treatment directives, contraindications, urgency cues, high-risk medications) combined with a relevance/grounding measure
Using controlled patient-facing prompts as safety stress tests for hallucination evaluation

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM hallucination severity using a novel risk-sensitive evaluation framework on controlled safety stress-test prompts, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
